mode: primary-source verification and direct implementation audit

sources.authors: Daniel A. Messenger and David M. Bortz
sources.title: Weak SINDy: Galerkin-Based Data-Driven Model Selection
sources.supports: Integration against compactly supported test functions moves the derivative onto the known test function. Quadrature, support, residual correlation, and nonlinear noise bias remain relevant.
sources.boundary: Original examples are autonomous ODEs. Extension to known-delay/input terms is a proposed weak-form identity and requires a newly specified identification problem; no published DLM-K noise guarantee is inferred.

sources.authors: Scott T. M. Dawson, Maziar S. Hemati, Matthew O. Williams and Clarence W. Rowley
sources.title: Characterizing and correcting for the effect of sensor noise in the dynamic mode decomposition
sources.read_locations: Sections 2.2-2.5, sensor-noise model, bias, corrected/forward-backward/TLS formulations
sources.supports: Sensor noise differs from process noise; noisy regressors can bias a fitted linear DMD operator; noise-aware identification exists.
sources.boundary: A result for linear DMD does not automatically extend to the nonlinear learned lift and AFT recurrence. The current supplemental experiment perturbs test inputs only and measures no identification bias.

implementation_evidence: CSTR holdout_generation.simulate_trajectory calls env.step(action, noise=True) and returns internal states without added sensor noise.
CSTR step adds process_noise*h inside each integration step before state bounding; observation_noise parameter is unused on this path.
Lorenz holdout generation is deterministic given the initial-history seed and contains no process or measurement noise.
DLM encoding concatenates the current observed state with learned features; the current-state projection also conditions the feature branch.
DLM encodes once, first transition has zero AFT correction, subsequent AFT contexts contain initial/predicted latent states only.
claim_boundaries: Fixed-checkpoint input sensitivity is separate from training on noisy measurements.
Prediction displacement is not the difference of two RMSE values.
No filtering or weak-form model is trained or claimed to improve these results.
One model-training seed and 12 trajectory/noise pairs do not establish robustness over training seeds or all noise processes.
The exact two-rollout difference equation does not imply contraction or monotone error growth.
